analysis.title: Major stock market rallies, do they continue today?
key_insights: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang after 10 days following pressure from President Trump, per Bloomberg. The decision was made quickly without consulting executive leadership beyond the board.
Nvidia stock rebounded 31% on the news after falling 50% since October 6. It remains down a net 31% from its peak.
Global equities reversed sharply. S&P 500 rose 4.7%, Nasdaq 6.5% and Sweden's OMXSPI 2.5%.
Asia followed this morning with Nikkei up 4% and KOSPI up 7%. Stock futures point to slight gains today.
Ten-year yields edged down slightly and two-year yields were unchanged or up a basis point or two.
The US dollar strengthened to 1.09, a level not seen since the turbulent days around Liberation Day. Crude oil fell below USD 90 per barrel, the lowest since late August.
Today's calendar includes the German Ifo survey and US consumer confidence. Yesterday's PMIs were mixed, with France weak and German manufacturing and services more positive on the near-term outlook.
Sweden: focus is on expectations of lower nominal bond supply when the SNDO releases its borrowing report on Thursday. Recent stock market jitters weighed on the SEK.
SEK December seasonality: PPM flows historically weakened the SEK, but the pattern has been less clear recently and the krona has tended to strengthen ahead of the flows.

Swedish politics: the Speaker holds talks at 9:30 AM ahead of a potential third prime ministerial vote. Red-green cooperation has taken a hit and the Centre Party is leaving the door slightly ajar to Kristersson. A new SvD/Demoskop poll puts the Moderates at their highest level in over ten years.
